To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the administration of CsA in vivo causes apoptosis in proximal tubule epithelial cells.
the renal tubular epithelial cells are the primary targets of CsA-induced toxicity.

the expression of miR-21 is elevated in human and mouse kidneys with chronic allograft dysfunction, and that miR-21 promotes tubular cell apoptosis by targeting the expression of the anti-apoptotic factor Bcl-2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of CsA on renal tubular epithelial cells.
the effects of the immunosuppressant cyclosporin on the renal tubular epithelial cells.
the effects of the immunosuppressant, cyclosporin a (CsA), on renal tubular epithelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cyclosporine is a nephrotoxic drug.
the use of cyclosporin in renal transplant recipients is associated with a significant increase in the risk of developing a malignancy.
cyclosporine A is a nephrotoxic drug that causes a decrease of renal blood flow, a decrease of GFR, an increase in tubular cell death, and an increase in tubulointerstitial fibrosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
renal epithelial cell death is an important contributor to renal injury.
the death of renal tubular epithelial cells is a major factor in the pathogenesis of cyclosporin (CsA)-related nephrotoxicity.
we are able to show that Csa causes renal tubular cell death and this cell death is definitely mediated by the mitochondrial pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cyclosporin a nephropathy is a disease of the proximal tubules.
the renal tubular epithelial cells are very sensitive to cyclosporin, and the mechanism is likely due to the accumulation of intracellular calcium.
the use of cyclosporin a is not a good idea.
